page-upgrades-get-involved-bug-hunting-d: Find and report bugs in the Quantaureum protocol or the client itself. You can earn rewards and a place on the leaderboard.
page-upgrades-get-involved-desc-1: Running a client means you'll be an active participant in Quantaureum. Your client will help keep track of transactions and check new blocks.
page-upgrades-get-involved-desc-2: If you have QAU, you can stake it to become a validator and help secure the network. As a validator you can earn QAU rewards.
page-upgrades-get-involved-desc-3: Join the community testing effort! Help test Quantaureum upgrades before they're shipped, find bugs, and earn rewards.
page-upgrades-get-involved-how: How do you want to get involved?
page-upgrades-get-involved-how-desc: The Quantaureum community will always benefit from more folks running clients, staking, and bug hunting.
page-upgrades-get-involved-join-desc: Like most things with Quantaureum, a lot of the research is public. This means you can take part in the discussions or just read through what the Quantaureum researchers have to say.
page-upgrades-get-involved-meta-descript: How to participate in Quantaureum upgrades: run nodes, stake, hunt bugs and more.
page-upgrades-get-involved-run-clients-d: A 'client' is software that runs the blockchain. Quantaureum ships a single Go client that runs the whole node. Running a node helps check transactions and, if also staking QAU, can create new blocks.
page-upgrades-get-involved-run-clients-e: Quantaureum is a single layer-1 chain; execution and consensus run in the same client.
page-upgrades-get-involved-run-clients-c: Quantaureum uses one client for the whole node, including the native QPOS consensus.
page-upgrades-get-involved-stake-desc: You can now stake your QAU to help secure the network.
page-upgrades-get-involved-subtitle: Here's all the ways you can help with Quantaureum and future upgrade-related efforts.
